correctness.rationale: For the lower-triangular optimal tableau A_ii=gamma_s, A_ij=delta_s (j<i), b_i=1/s, stage sums S_i satisfy a geometric recurrence with transfer t(z), yielding R_s(-x)=1-c_s+c_s t_s(x)^s. t_s strictly decreases from 1 to -q_s, so even s has unique stable endpoint t=-1 and odd s has unique endpoint t=-u_s, u_s^s=2/c_s-1, with no reentry. Algebra of delta/gamma yields the two explicit X_s, parity of stiff limits and X_s=4s²+O(1). Independently calculated the forward-substitution stability function for s=2..60 at six positive x per stage including both sides of the boundary; matches rational t^s expression and stability classification.
residual_risks: Assumes the exact published tableau, not floating-point implementation or general nonlinear stability; original reference numbering should be checked against the current arXiv version (source Theorem 5.3 versus assigned Theorem 5.2).

value.rationale: The real negative-axis absolute stability boundary is an operationally natural sharp quantitative property of the uniquely SSP-optimal implicit family. It distinguishes SSP radius from scalar stiffness stability and gives a full parity phase diagram, quadratic stage scaling and asymptotic non-damping of stiff modes—useful exact properties not mechanically settled by the SSP-optimality statement alone.
residual_risks: Applicability is limited to scalar linear decay (normal selfadjoint spectra by functional calculus), not general A-stability or SSP/TVD.

limitations: Best-of-knowledge originality; need bibliographic theorem-number correction in source metadata, but not scientific revision of correct formulas. No full complex stability proof.
